items.stem:
Two mathematically similar jugs are made of the same glass.
The smaller jug has height 15 cm and holds 900 cm3 of water when it is full.
The larger jug holds 3037.5 cm3 of water when it is full.

parts.t: Calculate the height of the larger jug.

A label on the smaller jug has area 84 cm2.
Calculate the area of the corresponding label on the larger jug.

Write down the ratio
    surface area of smaller jug : surface area of larger jug
in the form 1 : n.

sols: take the cube root, because volumes scale by the cube of the length scale factor
Area of the larger label = 84 × 2.25 = 189 cm2
The surface areas are in the ratio of the area scale factor.
ms:
M1 for 3037.5 ÷ 900 (= 3.375)
